a:r.a:t: Regulated enzymes often correspond to points in the pathways that have the same substrate and product, but a different enzyme.

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram illustrating opposing pathways of glycolysis and gluconeogenesis in rat liver. Glycolysis is outlined within a wide pink arrow going down, and gluconeogenesis is outlined within a wide blue arrow going up just next to the glycolysis arrow. The process begins with glucose, which is catalzyed by hexokinase, and irreversibly reacts with glucose 6-phophate. Glucose 6-phosphate is catalyzed by phosphohexose isomerase for a reversible reaction with fructose 6-phophate. Fructose 6-phosphate is catalzyed by phosphofructinase-1 for an irreversible reaction with fructose 1, 6-biphosphate. Fructose 1, 6-biphosphate is catalyzed by aldolase to react with dihydroxyacetone phosphate, which is catalyzed by triose phosphate isomerase for a reversible reaction with (2) glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate. (2) glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate is catalyzed by glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehrogenase for a reaction with (2) 1, 3-biphosphophoglycerate. (2) 1, 3 biphosphophoglycerate is catalyzed by phosphoglycerate kinase for a reaction with (2) 3-phosphoglycerate, which is catalyzed by phosphoglycerate mutase for a reaction with (2) 2-phosphoglycerate. (2) 2-phosphoglycerate is catalyzed by enolase for a reaction with phosphoenol-pyruvate, which is catalyzed by pyruvate kinase for an irreversible reaction with (2) pyruvate. This is the end of glycolysis. For gluconeogenesis, the arrow begins with (2)pyruvate, which is catalyzed by pyruvate carboxylase to iireversibly react with (2) oxaloacetate, which is catalyzed by PEP carboxykinase to react with (2) phosphoenol-pyruvate. The next four reactions from (2) phosphoenol-pyruvate to (2) glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate and the exact reverse of the reactions in glycolysis. Then for gluconeogenesis, (2) glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate is catalyzed by triose phosphate isomerase for a reversible reaction with dihydroxyacetone phosphate, which is catalyzed by aldolase to react with fructose 1, 6-biphosphate. Fructose 1, 6-biphosphate is then catalyzed by fructose 1, 6-biphosphatase-1 for an irreversible reaction with fructose 6-phosphate, which is catalyzed by phosphohexose isomerase to react with glucose 6-phosphate. Glucose 6-phosphate is then catalyzed by glucose 6-phosphate to react with glucose.
